divergence_help.NOT_MEASURED_HERE: Evidence lives outside this product, so nothing here bears on the claim.
divergence_help.NOT_APPLICABLE: Excluded with a justification. Nothing to reconcile.
divergence_help.CONSISTENT: The declaration and the measurement agree.

plugins.title: Plugins
plugins.subtitle: Your own analysers, packaged as container images and run during a scan beside Vectispire's scanners. Every account can read the registry; only the platform governor registers, changes or disables a plugin.
plugins.network_none: None — the container runs with the network cut.
plugins.no_delete: A plugin cannot be deleted, and its id never changes: the id is part of every issue it opened. Disable it to stop it everywhere; its activations are kept.
plugins.projects_none: No project. A plugin runs on nothing until a security lead switches it on for a project.
plugins.projects_hint: Switch it on or off from Solutions & projects.
plugins.id_permanent: The id can never be renamed or reused: it enters the fingerprint of every issue this plugin opens. 2 to 40 lowercase letters, digits and inner hyphens.
plugins.image_hint: Pinned by digest: repository@sha256: followed by 64 hex characters. A tag, even beside the digest, is refused.
plugins.languages_hint: The plugin runs only on a repository where one of these languages is present; elsewhere its step reads “not applicable”, which is not a failure.
plugins.arguments_hint: Handed to the image's entrypoint as a list, with no shell. {source} becomes /repo/source, {output} becomes /repo/output/ followed by the report file.
plugins.exit_codes_hint: Any other exit code fails the plugin's step and leaves its issues as they were. Exit 0 with an empty report means “analysed, found nothing”, and resolves every issue it opened on the repository.
plugins.network_hint: Off unless it genuinely must reach something, such as an internal rule mirror. The justification is recorded in the audit log.
plugins.signer_hint: Who must have signed the image, checked with cosign before it is pulled; an image it does not verify never runs. Keyless: the certificate identity and its OIDC issuer, both matched exactly. Or a public key. All empty: every executor that requires a signer — the default — refuses the plugin, unless the governor waives the requirement for it.
plugins.signer_none: None — refused wherever a signer is required, unless the governor waived it.
plugins.requirement_verified: Required: the declared signer is verified with cosign before every pull.
plugins.requirement_refused: Required, and no signer is declared: every executor that requires a signer — the default — refuses this plugin, so it runs nowhere.
plugins.waiver_with_signer: Its manifest declares a signer, which is verified all the same.
plugins.waive_explain: Executors refuse a plugin whose manifest declares no signer. A waiver lets this one plugin run unsigned from the next scan, on the built-in worker and on every agent. It is audited with its justification and forwarded to the SIEM. A signer the manifest declares is still verified.
plugins.waive_justification_hint: {{min}} to {{max}} characters: why the image cannot be signed yet, and by when it will be.
plugins.waived_notice: {{id}} runs unsigned from the next scan; the waiver is in the audit log.
plugins.waiver_revoked_notice: {{id}} no longer runs unsigned: from the next scan it is refused until its manifest declares a signer.
plugins.error_waive: The waiver could not be recorded.
plugins.error_revoke_waiver: The waiver could not be withdrawn.

plugins.error_exit_codes: The exit codes must be whole numbers separated by commas.
plugins.error_save: The plugin could not be saved.
plugins.error_enable: The plugin's state could not be changed.

plugins.updated_notice: {{id}} updated, manifest {{digest}}. Its issues and their triage are kept.
plugins.enabled_notice: {{id}} enabled: it runs from the next scan wherever it is switched on.
plugins.disabled_notice: {{id}} disabled: it runs nowhere from the next scan; its activations are kept.

sarif_sources.internal_only: Declare only a producer inside the organisation, which already has the code. For SARIF, the tool list is compared with each run's tool.driver.name: a report from any other tool is refused.
sarif_sources.slug_hint: Part of every imported issue's identity: name the producer, not the key. Declaring the same slug again with a new key continues the same backlog.
sarif_sources.key_placeholder: Choose a key holding the scopes the chosen kinds need

sarif_sources.scope_hint: Exactly one scope — a project or a repository, never the whole estate.
sarif_sources.tools_hint: Separated by commas, compared without regard to case.

checklist_templates.title: Checklist templates
checklist_templates.subtitle: Your organisation's security checklists, imported from its own workbooks. A workbook becomes a draft; its layout and answer words are confirmed on the sheet itself, its lines paired with the previous version, and only then is it published for projects to answer.
checklist_templates.error_load: Could not load the checklist templates.
checklist_templates.import_explain: The .xlsx is sent as it is and becomes the template's next version, as a draft: nothing is published in one step. A template has at most one draft at a time.
checklist_templates.slug_new_hint: A new slug creates the template: 1 to 64 lowercase letters, digits and inner hyphens.
checklist_templates.slug_existing_hint: This template exists: the workbook becomes its next version.
checklist_templates.file_hint: At most 10 MB. Macro-enabled workbooks (.xlsm) and the binary format are refused.
checklist_templates.too_large: The request body is larger than the {{limit}} bytes this route accepts.
checklist_templates.imported_notice: Version {{ordinal}} of "{{slug}}" imported as a draft. Confirm its layout below.
checklist_templates.column_header_row: Column header row found by the reader: {{row}}
checklist_templates.grid_legend: Blue: the item rows of the columns the layout names. Amber: the header cells. A column head names the field it holds; ƒ marks a formula.
checklist_templates.cells_truncated: The sheet has more cells than the preview shows: only the first 20,000 are drawn.
checklist_templates.layout_proposed_title: Layout (proposed by the reader, not confirmed)
checklist_templates.layout_explain: The reader proposed these from the workbook's structure — validation ranges, merged cells, runs of filled rows — never from its words. Check each column letter and each header cell against the grid, correct what is wrong, name the answer words, then confirm.
checklist_templates.header_explain: Each entry is a label cell the renderer leaves alone and a value cell it writes. Leave both empty when the template has no such entry.
checklist_templates.words_explain: The template's own words, whatever its language: which one means yes, which one no, and — only if this version offers it — which one means not applicable.
checklist_templates.words_none: The reader found no answer list it could read: type the template's words.
checklist_templates.word_na_hint: When the list has no such word, type one: the document will carry it, and the template's list is left as it is. A not applicable answer always needs its justification.
checklist_templates.confirm_clears_pairs: Confirming again reads the items anew and clears the pairs made by hand.
checklist_templates.evidence_explain: Say what proof a yes needs before a project's checklist can be submitted: none, a link or a file, or a file — and, for a proof that expires, for how many months it holds, 1 to 120; left empty, it does not expire. Only the lines you change are sent, on the revision on screen, and you become one of the draft's authors.
checklist_templates.evidence_kind_field: Proof asked by the item of row {{row}}
checklist_templates.evidence_months_field: Months a proof of the item of row {{row}} holds
checklist_templates.problem_evidence_months: A validity is a whole number of months from {{min}} to {{max}}, or left empty for a proof that does not expire.
checklist_templates.error_evidence: Could not set the proof the items ask for.
checklist_templates.refusal_not_draft: This version is no longer a draft: it is published or retired, and a published version never changes. To change it, derive a new draft from the published version.
checklist_templates.refusal_no_layout: This draft has no confirmed layout, so it has no items yet: confirm its layout first.
checklist_templates.refusal_changed: This version changed since you read it: you had revision {{revision}} on screen, and somebody else has edited, published or retired it since. Nothing was written over their change. Reload it, look at what changed, then try again.
checklist_templates.refusal_four_eyes_publish: You wrote this draft — you imported or derived it, confirmed its layout, paired its items or set what proof its lines ask for. Four-eyes approval is on, so a second person must publish it: another platform governor, administrator or CISO who did not write it. Written by: {{authors}}.
checklist_templates.refusal_four_eyes_retire: You wrote this version. Four-eyes approval is on, so a second person must retire it: another platform governor, administrator or CISO who did not write it. Written by: {{authors}}.
checklist_templates.refusal_retired: This version is already retired. Reload it to see where it stands.
checklist_templates.refusal_has_draft: This template already has a draft, and it has one at a time: publish that draft or set it aside before importing or deriving another version.
checklist_templates.refusal_not_published: A new draft is derived from a published version only, and this one is a draft or retired. Derive it from the template's published version instead.
checklist_templates.refusal_nothing_to_pair: This draft follows no published version, so there is nothing to pair its items with: every item is new.
checklist_templates.refusal_unrenderable: No sign-off could fill this draft's workbook in, so it was not published: cells Vectispire writes an answer, a comment or a header value into hold a formula other cells depend on — {{cells}}. In the workbook, un-share the formula — give each cell its own formula, or move it out of the cells the layout writes — then set this draft aside and import the corrected workbook as a new version.
checklist_templates.problem_sheet: Name the sheet the checklist is on.
checklist_templates.problem_required: Name the control, answer and comment columns: without them no item can be read nor an answer written.
checklist_templates.problem_letters: A column is named by its letters, from A to XFD.
checklist_templates.problem_rows: Name the first and the last item rows, the first at most the last.
checklist_templates.problem_header: A header entry names both cells — its label and its value, such as B3 — or neither.
checklist_templates.problem_words: Map the template's answer words to yes and no.
checklist_templates.problem_not_applicable: Name the word for not applicable, or stop offering it.
checklist_templates.pairing_none: No published version precedes this one: every item is new.
checklist_templates.pairing_explain: Each item against version {{ordinal}}: an unchanged item carries a project's answer as it is, a changed one carries it to be confirmed, an added one starts unanswered, a removed one's answer stays where it was given.
checklist_templates.pair_explain: Pair an added item with a removed one when they are the same control, reworded: the new item takes the old key, and a project's answer follows it, to be confirmed.
checklist_templates.publish_explain: Publishing makes this version what projects open their checklists on. A published version never changes: a new word, layout or binding is a new version, derived from it.
checklist_templates.publish_four_eyes: You wrote this draft, and four-eyes approval is on: it has to be published by a security lead (platform governor, administrator or CISO) who did not write it.
checklist_templates.publish_needs_layout: Confirm the layout before publishing: a draft without one has no items.
checklist_templates.confirm_publish: Publish revision {{revision}}, as shown on this page?
checklist_templates.confirm_set_aside: Set this draft aside? It will never be published.
checklist_templates.confirm_retire: Retire this version? No new checklist will open on it; those already on it stay readable.
checklist_templates.derive_explain: A derived draft keeps this version's workbook, layout and items, and is paired with this version.
checklist_templates.error_derive: Could not derive a new version.
checklist_templates.layout_confirmed_unpaired_one: Layout confirmed: {{count}} item read. The pairs made by hand were cleared — make them again if they still hold.
checklist_templates.layout_confirmed_unpaired_other: Layout confirmed: {{count}} items read. The pairs made by hand were cleared — make them again if they still hold.
checklist_templates.derived_notice: Version {{ordinal}} derived as a draft from version {{from}}.
checklist_templates.retired_notice: Version {{ordinal}} retired: no new checklist opens on it.
checklist_templates.aria_undo_rule: Undo the rule change on row {{row}}
checklist_templates.rules_title: What each line is measured by
checklist_templates.rules_explain: A line bound to a rule is measured on every project from the evidence Vectispire recorded — scans, imports — and people still answer it: the measurement stands beside the answer. The binding is part of the line: a line whose rule moved is changed against the previous version. Keep a rule per line, then save: only the lines changed are sent.
checklist_templates.rules_read_only: The rule each line is measured by is bound on a draft whose layout is confirmed, by a security lead. A published version never changes: derive a new one to bind other rules.
checklist_templates.rule_kpi: KPI, as the template writes it
checklist_templates.rule_no_kpi: The template states no KPI for this line.
checklist_templates.rule_kpi_hint: The KPI stays text: no number is read out of it. Compare it with what the rule measures, below, before keeping the rule.
checklist_templates.rule_unbound_explain: No rule: people answer the line, and nothing is measured beside it.
checklist_templates.rule_incomplete: The rule is not complete yet: each of its parameters is stated, none is assumed.
checklist_templates.rule_field_max_age: Maximum age of the evidence, in days
checklist_templates.rule_max_age_hint: {{min}} to {{max}}. Older evidence is no data, never a pass. Seven days are proposed; nothing else is.
checklist_templates.rule_schedule_yes: Must run at least as often as the maximum age
checklist_templates.rule_scope_other: A plugin or an imported tool
checklist_templates.rule_scope_hint: A plugin by its id, an imported tool by its declared source's slug and the tool's name as the source declares it. The list suggests the plugins and the SARIF sources' tools that exist.
checklist_templates.rule_thresholds_optional: Optional: what the open vulnerabilities may hold. A severity left blank is not judged.
checklist_templates.rule_thresholds_required: At least one severity: at most so many open, at least such a share resolved (settled triage left out of both), or both. A severity left blank is not judged.
checklist_templates.rule_field_minimum_ratio: Minimum coverage, above 0 and up to 1
checklist_templates.rule_pattern_hint: The suite's whole name: * for any run of characters, ? for one — com.example.arch.*. Several patterns, separated by commas, must each be met on their own suites: *Test, *IT for unit and functional tests. Skipped tests do not count; a failed or errored one fails the line.
checklist_templates.rule_change_review_hint: Read hourly through the forge connection that imported or discovered each repository: the forge's settings where it offers them (GitLab Premium and Ultimate, GitHub), otherwise the merge requests or pull requests merged in the window and who approved them — an approval by the author never counts. The maximum age is how old that reading may be.
checklist_templates.rule_coverage_scope_hint: Patterns over package paths, as the import keeps them: a JaCoCo or Cobertura package with its dots as slashes (org/example/service), an lcov file's directory. ** is any number of whole segments, * any characters within one; nothing else is a wildcard. Both blank measures the whole report. An import from before packages were kept has no data under a scope until the report is imported again.
checklist_templates.rule_components_legend: Packages required, at the versions allowed
checklist_templates.rule_components_hint: A version is allowed when it is written here, as the SBOM states it — or, on a pkg:maven/ package, when it is in a Maven range written here: [1.17,2.0), [1.17.7], (,2.0), read in Maven's order (1.17-SNAPSHOT before 1.17, 5.3.0.RELEASE equal to 5.3.0). A version the SBOM does not state is not judged.
checklist_templates.rule_components_present_hint: A package present whatever its version, including a version the SBOM does not state (managed by a BOM). A namespace — pkg:maven/org.example — asks for any of its packages, and the evidence lists each with its versions.

report_plugins.title: Report plugins
report_plugins.subtitle: Your organisation's own documents, rendered by your own container images from a project's export, then checked and signed by Vectispire. Governance readers see the registry; the platform governor registers, enables and withdraws; a security lead approves.
report_plugins.four_eyes_explained: With four-eyes on, a manifest waits — a new one, or a return to a digest approved earlier — until somebody other than the account that registered it approves that exact digest; turning four-eyes off afterwards does not let that account approve it. A report plugin's output leaves under the installation's key: one person deciding alone which code may produce signed documents is what four-eyes splits. Meanwhile the previously approved manifest keeps serving.
report_plugins.approved_alone: four-eyes was off: in effect at its registration
report_plugins.approve_four_eyes: You registered this digest, under four-eyes: somebody else who writes governance has to approve it, even if four-eyes has been turned off since.
report_plugins.no_delete: A report plugin cannot be deleted and its id is never reused: documents in the world name it. A wrong image is withdrawn; a fixed image is a new manifest.
report_plugins.manifest_hint: Paste the manifest. The image is pinned by digest, the signer is required, the document's type is one of the closed list. The server checks it again and has the last word.
report_plugins.withdraw_explain: The digest never runs again and cannot be registered again. The documents it produced stay stored, as evidence of what was handed out. If it is the approved digest, the plugin has none until a new manifest is approved.

connections.ca_hint: The CA that issued the server's certificate, when it is not a public one. It is trusted for this connection alone; the host name is still checked.
connections.probe_explained: The token is presented to the forge once before anything is kept. The connection is refused when the forge rejects the token or it has expired, when it holds a scope outside the read-only ones, when the server is older than GitLab 16 or GitHub Enterprise Server 3.12, when the owner is unknown, or when the address is blocked — internal without the statement above, or reserved. The reason is shown here.
connections.refused: The forge or the outbound guard refused this connection:
connections.ca_unpin: Unpin the CA and use the public CAs
connections.reprobe_hint: Changing the network statement or the CA presents the stored token again before anything is saved.
connections.rotate_explained: The new token of {{name}} is checked like a new one. The connection keeps its discoveries and the provenance of its imported targets.
connections.delete_confirm_one: Delete {{name}}? Its discoveries, and the provenance of the target imported through it, go with it. The target itself is kept: an imported repository is a target like any other.
connections.delete_confirm_other: Delete {{name}}? Its discoveries and the provenance of its {{count}} imported targets go with it. The targets themselves are kept: an imported repository is a target like any other.

discovery.error_load: The connection could not be loaded.
discovery.error_request: The discovery could not be requested.
discovery.error_poll: The discovery's progress could not be read; trying again shortly.
discovery.error_changes: The repositories could not be loaded.
discovery.title: Discovery
discovery.subtitle: Lists the repositories the token can see and compares them with the previous discovery. Nothing is imported at this step.
discovery.in_progress: Discovery #{{id}} is already running for this connection.
discovery.unsupported: This version does not yet discover the repositories of a GitHub; GitLab only.
discovery.pending: Waiting for a control-plane instance to take it — usually a few seconds.
discovery.running: Listing. This page follows it by itself.
discovery.skipped_explained: A repository whose id, path or name does not fit is not kept, and counted here.
discovery.reset_at: The limit lifts at {{date}}: run the discovery again then.
discovery.partial_explained: What was listed is kept and can be imported. Nothing is marked gone: a partial listing proves nothing about what it did not reach.

reason.time_bound: Stopped after thirty minutes. Discover again to continue.
reason.rate_limited: The forge's rate limit asked for a longer wait than a discovery spends.
reason.token_rejected: The forge rejected the token: it is wrong, expired or revoked. Replace it.
reason.destination_blocked: The outbound guard blocked the address: it now resolves where this connection may not go.
reason.cross_origin_page: The forge pointed to a next page on another address. Nothing was sent there, and the run stopped.
reason.forge_unavailable: The forge did not answer after three attempts.
reason.forge_refused: The forge refused a listing: the token needs the read_api scope and the Reporter role.
reason.connection_unusable: The connection cannot be used as stored: its token no longer decrypts, or its pinned CA has expired.
reason.unsupported: This version does not list this forge's repositories.
reason.executor_lost: The instances running it stopped answering three times.
reason.internal_error: An unexpected error stopped it; the server's log has the rest.

discovery.gone_not_counted: Gone is not counted: only a completed discovery says which repositories are no longer listed.
discovery.gone_kept: A repository gone or archived on the forge is not deleted from Vectispire: its target, if imported, keeps its history.

selection.title: Choose the repositories
selection.subtitle: From discovery #{{id}}. What is imported is what is ticked, never what a filter matches.
selection.error_load: The repositories could not be loaded.
selection.superseded: A newer discovery (#{{id}}) has ended: the choice now reads that one, and the ticks were cleared.
selection.not_selectable: This discovery has not ended completed or partial: there is nothing to choose from yet.
selection.path_hint: A pattern — * any run of characters, ? one — or, without either, a search.
selection.unjudged_title: Values the forge did not give:
selection.unjudged_archived_one: archived: {{count}} repository the forge did not say
selection.unjudged_archived_other: archived: {{count}} repositories the forge did not say
selection.unjudged_fork_one: fork: {{count}} repository whose source the forge did not name
selection.unjudged_fork_other: fork: {{count}} repositories whose source the forge did not name
selection.unjudged_activity_one: last activity: {{count}} repository with none given
selection.unjudged_activity_other: last activity: {{count}} repositories with none given
selection.unjudged_explained: A filter that hides keeps a repository it cannot judge; a filter that requires a value leaves it out.
selection.operations_explained: These apply to every repository the filters match, on every page. Proposed ticks the selectable ones that are not archived, not forks and not in a personal namespace.
selection.by_id: Forge ids, separated by commas or spaces
selection.dropped_one: {{count}} id could not be ticked: it is already a target, empty, or not in this discovery.
selection.dropped_other: {{count}} ids could not be ticked: they are already targets, empty, or not in this discovery.

mapping.title: Where they are filed
mapping.explained: Proposed from the forge's groups. An existing solution or project of the same name is reused, never renamed. A change applies to the namespace and everything below it, or to one repository.

import.title: Place and import
import.batch_bound: {{count}} are selected and an import takes at most {{max}}: the first {{max}} are imported now, the rest stay ticked for the next import.
import.credentials_explained: Per host. The connection's own token never clones. An SSH key clones over SSH, an HTTPS token bound to the host over HTTPS; with none, a private repository's scans fail with "requires authentication".
import.first_scan_toggle: Scan each new target once now
import.first_scan_hint: Off by default: otherwise each target is scanned at its own slot of the default schedule. When on, the scans are spaced so that they reach the forge one at a time.
import.stale: Something changed since the preview: preview again before importing.
import.error_preview: The preview could not be computed.
import.will_refuse_one: {{count}} repository refused — the import would be refused whole
import.will_refuse_other: {{count}} repositories refused — the import would be refused whole
import.schedule_one: No schedule of their own: the default applies, every day, each target at its own slot.
import.schedule_other: No schedule of their own: the default applies, every {{count}} days, each target at its own slot.
import.first_scans_planned_other: {{count}} first scans, one every {{spacing}} s, from {{from}} to {{to}}.
import.no_first_scans: No first scan: each target waits for its slot.
import.no_grant: No grant is created: granting stays on its own screen.
import.refused_explained: The server's reason for each. Fix the filing above, or untick them.
import.project_reused_one: Project {{name}}: existing, reused — {{count}} target; granted to accounts: {{accounts}}, teams: {{teams}}
import.project_reused_other: Project {{name}}: existing, reused — {{count}} targets; granted to accounts: {{accounts}}, teams: {{teams}}
import.project_created_one: Project {{name}}: created, no grant yet — {{count}} target
import.project_created_other: Project {{name}}: created, no grant yet — {{count}} targets
import.visible_everyone: Every signed-in account: visibility is not restricted on this installation.
import.visible_unfiled: Administrators and the roles that see the whole estate only: it is filed into no project.
import.visible_new_project: Administrators and the roles that see the whole estate only: project {{project}} is new and nobody holds a grant on it yet.
import.visible_no_grant: Administrators and the roles that see the whole estate only: nobody holds a grant on project {{project}}.
import.visible_granted: Administrators and the roles that see the whole estate, plus those granted project {{project}} — accounts: {{accounts}}, teams: {{teams}}.
import.blocked: The import is refused whole while a repository is refused: fix its filing or untick it.

result.title: Imported
result.audit: Each target, solution and project is in the audit log, and the import is summarised there once as "{{operation}}".
